chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Bundar, who said: We were narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Sulayman ibn 'Amr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever prays on the night of the middle of the month of Ramadan with one hundred rak'ahs, reciting

key_terms.أَعْدَاءَهُ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ: His enemies from jinn and humans
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ النِّصْفِ: The night of the middle (15th night)
key_terms.يُؤْمِنُونَهُ مِنَ النَّارِ: They secure him from the Fire

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and angelic protections for praying on the night of the 15th of Ramadan?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration links the specific devotional practice of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas ten times per unit to the intercession of angels during the critical moments of death. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the 15th of Ramadan (Laylat al-Bara'ah) as a time for securing divine protection from both visible and invisible adversaries, reinforcing the spiritual efficacy of consistent Quranic recitation.
